name: Salesforce
description: CRM and Sales: the leading enterprise CRM platform covering sales, service, marketing and analytics with a broad API surface.
access_notes: Free Developer Edition org is self-serve at developer.salesforce.com/signup and never expires with periodic login. Note: creation of new Connected Apps is restricted as of Spring '26; new integrations self-serve via External Client Apps instead, which remain creatable in Dev Edition orgs.
mcp_notes: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers went GA on April 29, 2026 (Enterprise Edition and above, plus Developer Edition); auth via External Client App with mcp_api scope and OAuth+PKCE. Composio also has a SALESFORCE toolkit (223 tools, 7 triggers, OAuth2 managed auth).
uncertainty_notes: No generic HTTP webhooks product; event push is via Outbound Messages, Platform Events/Streaming, and the gRPC Pub/Sub API, so supports_webhooks left null. GraphQL API and Pub/Sub (gRPC) API are documented in the developer portal but I did not capture dedicated evidence URLs for them.

evidence.note: Enable OAuth Settings for API Integration: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (with PKCE), client credentials flow, and other flows configured on connected/external client apps.
REST API developer guide intro ties REST API access to OAuth and connected apps.
'It's a free Salesforce org... sign up at developer.salesforce.com/signup' — free self-serve Developer Edition that does not expire with 6-monthly login.
Official Salesforce blog: hosted MCP servers generally available, fully managed, OAuth + PKCE via External Client Apps.
Composio SALESFORCE toolkit page: OAUTH2/S2S_OAUTH2, 223 tools, 7 triggers, Composio managed app available.

verifier-supplied evidence: All four protocols confirmed live, but the draft admitted it had no dedicated evidence URLs for GraphQL and gRPC. GraphQL API guide and gRPC-based Pub/Sub API docs found independently.

name: HubSpot
description: CRM and Sales: inbound marketing, sales and service platform with a free CRM tier and extensive CRM object APIs.
access_notes: Free HubSpot CRM accounts and free developer accounts are self-serve. OAuth apps are required for multi-account distribution; private apps issue a static bearer access token for a single account (super admin required to create one).
mcp_notes: HubSpot offers two official MCP servers: a remote hosted CRM MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE via an MCP auth app) and a local developer MCP server via the HubSpot CLI / @hubspot/mcp-server npm package. Composio also has a HUBSPOT toolkit (245 tools, 2 triggers).
uncertainty_notes: Private app access tokens are 'implemented on top of OAuth' and sent as Bearer tokens; classified as bearer_token. Some API scopes/endpoints are gated by paid account tiers, but core CRM objects work on the free tier.

evidence.note: Authentication overview: OAuth required for multi-account apps; static auth access tokens (private apps) for single-account installs.
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with client ID/secret and scopes; app creation is self-serve in a developer account.
Private app access tokens used as 'Authorization: Bearer [YOUR_TOKEN]' against HubSpot REST API endpoints (e.g. Contacts API).
Official page describing HubSpot's two MCP servers: remote CRM MCP server at mcp.hubspot.com and the local developer MCP server.
Composio HUBSPOT toolkit page: OAUTH2/API_KEY, 245 tools, 2 triggers, Composio managed app available.
Webhooks journal and management APIs (v4) for subscribing to real-time CRM events; also documents OAuth client-credentials tokens for app-level auth.

name: Pipedrive
description: CRM and Sales: pipeline-focused sales CRM for SMBs with deals, contacts, activities and a full REST API on every plan.
access_notes: Every Pipedrive plan includes an API token giving free REST API access; Pipedrive itself is a paid product with a self-serve free trial. Developers can also get a free developer sandbox account at developers.pipedrive.com and register apps in Developer Hub for OAuth credentials.
mcp_notes: Pipedrive launched its native hosted MCP server (mcp.pipedrive.ai) on June 30, 2026, available on all plans via OAuth. Composio has a PIPEDRIVE toolkit (402 tools, 3 triggers, OAuth2/API key); Composio managed app listed as not available, so bring-your-own OAuth credentials.
uncertainty_notes: API token is tied to a single user/company and only one can be active at a time. OAuth client_id/client_secret are sent via HTTP Basic auth only during token exchange, not as an API auth method.

evidence.note: All requests need authentication: API token in x-api-token header for personal integrations, or OAuth 2.0 for apps.
OAuth 2.0 is the recommended protocol for Marketplace apps; step 1 is 'Get your developer sandbox account' at developers.pipedrive.com — self-serve.
'Every Pipedrive plan comes with an API token that gives you access to our RESTful API for free... Access what you need via webhooks, API endpoints... hundreds of endpoints.'
Official newsroom announcement (June 30, 2026): native hosted MCP server on all plans, OAuth connection, built and maintained by Pipedrive.
Composio PIPEDRIVE toolkit page: OAUTH2/API_KEY, 402 tools, 3 triggers; Composio managed app not available.

name: Attio
description: CRM and Sales: modern, data-model-flexible CRM for teams with a REST API, webhooks and a hosted MCP server on all plans.
access_notes: Free plan (up to 3 seats) includes API and webhook access; single-workspace API keys are generated self-serve in workspace developer settings, and OAuth apps are registered self-serve at build.attio.com. New workspaces get a 14-day Pro trial.
mcp_notes: Attio hosts an official remote MCP server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp (OAuth login, all plans, read auto-approved / writes need confirmation). Composio also has an ATTIO toolkit (108 tools, 0 triggers, OAuth2 managed app).
uncertainty_notes: HTTP Basic auth is supported only as an alternative way to pass the token (token as username); Bearer is recommended. Composio toolkit currently lists 0 triggers even though Attio's API supports webhooks.

evidence.note: Two ways to get an access token: OAuth 2.0 flow for multi-workspace apps, or a self-generated single-workspace API key; tokens passed as Authorization: Bearer (Basic auth also supported).
'Apps in Attio's App Store and access to Attio's API are available on all Attio plans' — including the Free plan (up to 3 seats).
Webhooks can be created via settings or the API, with event subscriptions and filtering (V2 webhooks).
Official docs for Attio MCP: hosted server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp using OAuth, works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor.
Composio ATTIO toolkit page: OAuth2, 108 tools, Composio managed app available.

name: Twenty
description: CRM and Sales: open-source, self-hostable CRM ('open alternative to Salesforce') with schema-generated REST and GraphQL APIs and a built-in MCP server.
access_notes: Open-source and self-hostable for free via Docker Compose; Twenty Cloud workspaces are self-serve sign-up. API keys are generated in Settings -> API & Webhooks; OAuth clients register dynamically via RFC 7591 (no dashboard approval).
mcp_notes: Vendor MCP server is built into the product at {workspace-url}/mcp (streamable-http, OAuth or API key). Several community MCP wrappers exist on npm/GitHub. No Composio toolkit found: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/twenty returns 404 and web search found no Composio Twenty toolkit page.
uncertainty_notes: primary_auth: API key is the documented default for scripts/integrations; OAuth (auth code + PKCE, client credentials) is recommended for external multi-user apps, so either could be considered primary. API is schema-per-tenant (no static reference). Searched for a Composio Twenty toolkit (docs.composio.dev/toolkits/twenty and web search) and found none.

evidence.note: REST (/rest/) and GraphQL (/graphql/) core + metadata APIs generated from the workspace schema; auth via 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' created in Settings -> API & Webhooks.
OAuth 2.0 authorization code + PKCE for user-facing apps and client credentials for server-to-server, with dynamic client registration (RFC 7591).
Official repo: '#1 Open-Source CRM', cloud sign-up at twenty.com or self-host with Docker Compose.
Official docs: MCP server built in at https://{workspace-url}/mcp for cloud and self-hosted, with OAuth (recommended) or API key auth.

name: Podio
description: CRM and Sales: Progress Podio is a customizable work-management/CRM platform of apps, items and workspaces with a full REST API.
access_notes: Free plan (up to 5 employees, 100 items, 1,000 API calls/day) with no credit card; API keys (client ID/secret) are self-serve from account settings at podio.com. Higher API capacity requires paid plans/add-ons under the Aug 2026 hybrid pricing model.
mcp_notes: Progress (Podio's vendor) documents an official Podio MCP Server for ChatGPT, Copilot Studio, Claude etc., usable with shared default credentials or your own Podio API key. No Composio Podio toolkit found (docs.composio.dev/toolkits/podio and composio.dev/toolkits/podio both 404); Composio only has a toolkit for Procfu, a third-party Podio automation product.
uncertainty_notes: 'custom' covers Podio's non-standard OAuth grants: username/password grant and 'app authentication' (app_id + app_token), plus a client-side implicit flow. Access token is sent as 'Authorization: OAuth2 TOKEN' rather than standard Bearer. Free-plan API is capped at 1,000 calls/day and add-ons cannot be purchased on free plans.

evidence.note: OAuth2 with server-side, client-side, password and app-authentication flows; app registration yields Client ID/Secret; 'Authorization: OAuth2 ACCESS_TOKEN' header.
'Get started right away - generate your API key'; 'the entire Podio frontend is built on the API'; 'you have the ability to register webhooks in your Podio apps'.

name: Zoho CRM

access_notes: Free Edition (3 users, free forever) includes REST API access with 5,000 API credits/day; app registration in the Zoho API Console is self-serve, and a free Developer Edition org exists for testing. No API key option — OAuth 2.0 only, with a 'Self Client' console option for server-side/standalone use.
mcp_notes: Zoho offers official pre-built Zoho CRM MCP servers (four scoped servers: Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, Workflow Automation) hosted by Zoho and authenticated via OAuth, part of the wider Zoho MCP product. Composio has a ZOHO toolkit (57 tools, category crm, OAuth2 managed app) covering Zoho CRM.
uncertainty_notes: Access token is passed as 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {token}' rather than standard Bearer, and endpoints are region-specific (zohoapis.com/.eu/.in etc.). The Self Client console flow is a Zoho-specific way to mint OAuth grant tokens, not a separate auth method. Composio toolkit slug is ZOHO (suite-level) rather than a CRM-specific slug.

evidence.note: Zoho CRM API uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication; access tokens valid 1 hour with long-lived refresh tokens.
Authorization code grant flow via accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/auth, plus Self Client option in the Zoho Developer Console.
API credit table: Free Edition gets 5,000 credits per 24-hour window (concurrency 5) — API is available on the free edition.
Free Edition, 'free forever for 3 users', lists 'APIs — Connect Zoho CRM to any app and perform actions with 5000 API calls/day'.
Notification APIs push instant notifications to a provided URL on record create/update/delete — webhook-style event delivery.
Official Zoho CRM MCP docs: four pre-built vendor-hosted MCP servers usable from Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Windsurf via OAuth.

name: Close
description: CRM and Sales: sales-focused CRM with built-in calling, email and SMS, exposing a full REST API over leads, contacts, opportunities and activities.
access_notes: No free plan; self-serve 14-day free trial with no credit card at app.close.com/signup (paid plans from $9-19/user/month). API keys are self-serve under Settings -> Developer -> API Keys; OAuth apps can be created for user-facing integrations.
mcp_notes: Close hosts an official MCP server at https://mcp.close.com/mcp (HTTP Streamable, OAuth 2.0 with Dynamic Client Registration, or Close-API-Key + Close-Scope headers with mcp.read / mcp.write_safe / mcp.write_destructive scopes). Composio has a CLOSE toolkit, though it is narrow (6 tools, 0 triggers, API key auth).
uncertainty_notes: API keys are transmitted via HTTP Basic auth (key as username, blank password) — mechanism is Basic, credential type is api_key. The Composio toolkit exists but covers only a handful of actions relative to the full Close API.

evidence.note: Base URL https://api.close.com/api/v1; two auth methods: API keys (Basic auth, key as username) and OAuth 2.0 'best for user-facing integrations'.
API keys created self-serve under Settings -> Developer -> API Keys, scoped to a user/organization.
'Start your free 14-day trial — no credit card required'; four paid tiers, no permanent free plan.
Webhook subscriptions POST event data (create/update/delete on leads, opportunities, etc.) with HMAC signatures and retries.
Official Close MCP server at https://mcp.close.com/mcp with OAuth 2.0 DCR or Close-API-Key/Close-Scope header auth and three scope tiers.
Composio CLOSE toolkit page: API_KEY auth, 6 tools, 0 triggers, category crm.

name: Copper
description: CRM and Sales: Google Workspace-native CRM for managing people, companies, leads, opportunities and pipelines.
access_notes: 14-day free trial, no credit card; no permanent free plan. API keys are self-serve in-app (Settings > Integrations > API Keys, admin users). OAuth2 app registration requires contacting Copper to obtain client_id/client_secret. Pricing page implies API/integrations are bundled at Professional tier and above.
mcp_notes: No official vendor MCP found in Copper docs and no Composio toolkit page (docs.composio.dev/toolkits/copper returns 404). Community MCP servers exist (e.g. hasankhadra/copper-mcp on GitHub, AnythingMCP connector).
uncertainty_notes: OAuth2 client registration is 'contact us' rather than a self-serve developer portal, but API-key auth is fully self-serve so this does not block building. Exact plan tier at which the Developer API is enabled was inferred from the pricing page feature list ('Integrations' at Professional) and a third-party pricing review, not from an explicit official statement.

evidence.note: Two ways to access the API: self-serve API keys (System settings > API Keys) and OAuth2.0, 'the preferred approach for partner integrations'.
OAuth2.0 Authorization Code Grant; app registration requires contacting Copper for client_id/client_secret; single developer/v1/all scope with full read and modify access.
Copper Developer API is a RESTful interface with JSON responses at api.copper.com/developer_api/ covering most Copper resources.

Official pricing page: Basic/Professional/Business tiers, no free plan; 'Try Copper free' trial with instant activation and no credit card; 'API & Embedded integration SDK' appears in the plan feature-comparison table under Integrations.
Official Dev API docs; the API includes webhook CRUD endpoints under /developer_api/v1/webhooks (confirmed via docs navigation and integrator references).
Community MCP server explicitly labeled 'Unofficial'; no vendor MCP announced in Copper docs; docs.composio.dev/toolkits/copper returns 404.

name: DealCloud
description: CRM and Sales: Intapp's deal and relationship management platform for private equity, investment banking and advisory firms.
access_notes: No self-serve signup or public pricing; Intapp DealCloud is sold via demo/sales (enterprise contracts). For existing customers, an admin must enable the 'API' capability on a user group, then the user self-serves an API key from their Profile; that API key is used as the client_secret in the OAuth2 client-credentials token flow. The MCP server additionally requires the 'DealCloud with Celeste' license.
mcp_notes: Official DealCloud MCP Server in client preview starting July 2026; read-only access to DealCloud data, per-user OAuth sign-in, requires DealCloud with Celeste license plus 'MCP Access' user permission. No Composio toolkit found (docs.composio.dev/toolkits/dealcloud returns 404).
uncertainty_notes: No push webhooks: real-time events are delivered via the stateful Publications API (long-polling of topics), so supports_webhooks is recorded as false even though event-driven integration is possible. API is customer-gated: credentials exist only inside a purchased DealCloud site, so verdict buildable_now applies to firms that already have a license.

evidence.note: 'DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token'; scopes for data, user_management, publish, ri_import, backup; tokens expire after 15 minutes.
API access requires a user group with the 'API' capability enabled by an admin; the user then enables and copies an API key from their Profile.
Official 'DealCloud MCP Server — client preview starting July 2026' documented by the vendor; gives AI assistants read access scoped to the user's permissions.
MCP prerequisites: 'DealCloud with Celeste license', admin 'Manage MCP Servers' and end-user 'MCP Access' permissions; per-user OAuth sign-in, no client_id/secret needed.
Real-time events via the stateful Publications API (poll-based topic consumption, 9-day retention) rather than push webhooks; standard REST Data/Schema/User Management APIs also documented.
Intapp offers only 'Schedule a demo' / speak-with-an-expert; no self-serve signup or public pricing for DealCloud.

name: Zendesk
description: Support and Helpdesk: customer service platform with ticketing, help center, messaging and AI agents.
access_notes: Self-serve free trial of Zendesk Suite (no permanent free plan). API tokens are generated in Admin Center by admins; OAuth clients are registered per instance. Zendesk is pushing existing API-token users to migrate to OAuth. Global OAuth clients (for multi-customer apps) require a request to Zendesk.
mcp_notes: Zendesk announced both an MCP client (GA) and a first-party Zendesk MCP Server (early access, per-tenant at <subdomain>.zendesk.com/api/mcp with OAuth) at Relate 2026. Composio Zendesk toolkit exists at docs.composio.dev/toolkits/zendesk. Multiple community MCP servers also exist (e.g. fruggr/zendesk-mcp-server).
uncertainty_notes: The vendor MCP Server was in early access ('early access this summer', Relate 2026 newsroom); GA status not confirmed on an official page. GraphQL/websocket apply to specific surfaces (e.g. Chat/streaming APIs); the core Support API is REST.

evidence.note: OAuth access tokens (Bearer) recommended; legacy API tokens use Basic auth with {email}/token:{api_token}; existing token users must migrate to OAuth.
Zendesk supports two OAuth flows: authorization code (per-user) and client credentials (server-to-server).
API tokens created self-serve in Admin Center; OAuth clients registered per instance; permissions scoped by user role and OAuth scopes.
Official announcement of Zendesk MCP Client and Zendesk MCP Server ('connect Zendesk tickets, knowledge, and other data to external AI systems'), server in early access.
Composio Zendesk toolkit page exists (fetched successfully).
Zendesk webhooks API is a documented core feature for subscribing to ticket and other events.

name: Intercom
description: Support and Helpdesk: customer messaging and support platform with shared inbox, help center and the Fin AI agent.
access_notes: Self-serve signup with a free trial (no permanent free plan); developers get an Access Token immediately upon creating an app in the Developer Hub on their own workspace. Public apps that access other customers' workspaces must use OAuth and go through app review for scope approval.
mcp_notes: Intercom hosts an official remote MCP server (https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp for US, https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp for EU; AU not yet supported) with OAuth or Bearer token auth, documented at developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp and github.com/intercom/intercom-mcp-server. Composio Intercom toolkit exists at docs.composio.dev/toolkits/intercom.
uncertainty_notes: OAuth tokens have no fixed expiry and Intercom does not issue refresh tokens; re-authorization is needed if revoked. Public-app OAuth scopes are reviewed at app submission, which adds a review step for multi-tenant integrations but does not gate private-app API access.

evidence.note: Access Token issued as soon as you create an app on your workspace (private apps); OAuth required for public apps accessing other people's Intercom data; tokens sent as Authorization: Bearer.
OAuth authorization-code flow with client_id/client_secret from the Developer Hub; regional endpoints for US/EU/AU.
REST API at api.intercom.io covering contacts, conversations, tickets, companies, articles etc.; self-serve workspace setup for developers.
Official Intercom-hosted remote MCP server at mcp.intercom.com/mcp (US) and mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp (EU), following the authenticated remote MCP spec.
Composio Intercom toolkit page exists (fetched successfully).
'Webhook topics are related to corresponding OAuth permission scopes' — webhooks are a documented platform feature tied to scopes.

name: Freshdesk

Each agent gets a personal API key from Profile Settings (revealed after captcha), used as the Basic-auth username with any dummy password. API access was not available on the legacy free 'Sprout' plan; availability on the current Free plan not confirmed from official docs.

uncertainty_notes: v2 API has no OAuth flow for standard server-to-server use (OAuth exists only for Freshworks Marketplace app scenarios). Official vendor MCP is gated behind Enterprise-plan EAP, but the REST API itself is self-serve. API availability on the current Free plan tier is unverified.

evidence.note: Official: API key retrieved self-serve from agent Profile Settings > View API key; activities via API follow the agent's role permissions.
Official developer docs: REST API v2 at https://<domain>.freshdesk.com/api/v2/ using HTTP Basic Auth with the API key as username.
Official note: 'If your account is on the Sprout plan, the API key and the API functionality will NOT be available' — API access is plan-dependent.
Official Freshworks MCP server for Freshdesk, 'currently in Beta ... EAP for selected customers on the Enterprise plan'; tools include ticket, conversation and solution-article operations.
Composio Freshdesk toolkit page exists; requires user-provided Basic Auth credentials.
Freshdesk supports webhooks triggered from automation rules, documented in the official developer docs.

name: Front
description: Support and Helpdesk: shared-inbox customer communication platform combining email, messaging channels and team collaboration.
access_notes: Self-serve product trial, plus free developer accounts offered via the developer portal for building/testing. API tokens are created self-serve in Settings > Developers. OAuth (authorization code, with refresh tokens) is required for public integrations distributed via the Front App Store; API tokens are fine for private integrations.
mcp_notes: Official first-party Front MCP server in open beta at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, user-scoped permissions; Claude directory listing available; free during open beta). No Composio Front toolkit found: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/front and composio.dev/toolkits/frontapp return 404, and composio.dev/toolkits/front falls back to a category page.

OAuth authorization-code flow at app.frontapp.com/oauth/authorize and /oauth/token; access tokens last 60 minutes, refresh tokens 6 months.
API tokens created self-serve under Settings > Developers > API Tokens; getting-started guide also points to free developer accounts.
Official Front MCP server (open beta) at mcp.frontapp.com/mcp; OAuth-authenticated, user-scoped authorization.
Developer portal lists Core API (REST), MCP Server, Connectors, Plugin SDK and Channel API; Core API supports webhook-based event notifications via application webhooks and rules.

name: Pylon

Once a customer, Admin users generate API bearer tokens self-serve in Settings > API Tokens; the MCP server uses per-user OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit) and needs the 'MCP Access' role.

Only Admin users can create API tokens; API covers accounts, contacts, issues, messages, tasks, knowledge base, custom objects etc.; webhooks configured via Settings > Webhooks and Triggers with 'Send webhook' actions.
Official Pylon MCP Server at https://mcp.usepylon.com, OAuth 2.0 (AuthKit), streamable HTTP, read/write tools for issues, accounts, contacts, scoped to the user's dashboard permissions.
Official get-started page is a 'Schedule a personalized 30-minute demo' form; no self-serve signup path.
Official developer docs: REST API at api.usepylon.com with a full API reference across Pylon objects.

Official REST API section covering API v1 (legacy) and API v3 (current) with documentation and examples.
Official built-in MCP server at https://<account>/api/mcp, streamable HTTP, Bearer token or OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE), acting under the agent's identity.

name: Plain

Plans from $35/seat/month, 7-day free trial, no credit card required — self-serve trial signup.
Webhook targets (up to 25 per workspace) deliver workspace events via HTTPS POST.
Official Plain MCP server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp using OAuth with the user's existing Plain account.

name: Help Scout
description: Support and helpdesk: shared-inbox customer support platform (conversations, customers, mailboxes/inboxes, Docs knowledge base).
